decisive_spans.text: A 45-year-old man presented with a 5-day history of an abrupt onset of an asymptomatic cutaneous eruption on the neck and both forearms
He denied fever, malaise, or other constitutional symptoms
A punch biopsy showed no epidermal changes and revealed a dense inflammatory neutrophilic infiltrate within the dermis
a white-cell count of 13,000/mm3 with 89% neutrophils

response.rationale: D4 is strongly supported by the acute onset of asymptomatic cutaneous eruption, progressive enlargement of lesions, dense inflammatory neutrophilic infiltrate, and elevated white cell count with neutrophilia. While D1 also has support for neutrophilic infiltrate and neutrophilia, the description of the lesions with a central depression mimicking vesiculation contradicts the typical presentation of neutrophilic urticaria. D2 and D3 have less specific support and do not encompass the full clinical picture as well as D4.
